title: Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet
scenario: Orrin Genomics' sequencing lab pushes about 10 TB of run data to AWS every night inside a 6-hour window, so the transfer must sustain roughly 4 Gbps for analysis to start at 06:00. A two-week trial over the public internet showed throughput falling to 1.5 Gbps at busy times, and the transfer tool aborts if the rate stays below 3 Gbps for 5 minutes. The data-protection policy requires encryption in transit for all lab data, the research director needs a pilot to start within five days, and the network provider quotes several weeks for any new physical circuit. The lab has budget for one physical circuit only, and the link must still work if that circuit fails.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
The research director needs a pilot flowing within five days, before any new physical circuit can be delivered
The data-protection officer requires encryption in transit for all lab data on every path
Finance funds one physical circuit only, so resilience cannot come from a second circuit
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented
Steady-state path is sized above the stated 4 Gbps and does not show the 1.5 Gbps dips measured on the internet
Five-day pilot, encryption in transit and the failure-of-the-circuit requirement are each met by a named path

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
